# Relics, documents and keepsakes

Every relic is earned by learning, never by time spent. Their stories are part of the lore.

## Artifacts

Things the city gave back to you, one for every district restored.

- **The Brass Lantern**: Old and dented, with a little door of smoked glass. Wren handed it to you on your first morning, cold as a stone from a stream. A Warden's lamp lights for whoever truly remembers.
- **Wren's Notecard**: One small white card from the snowdrift on the Archive floor, picked up by a clerk who said she had better learn with you. It is blank on both sides. That was rather the point.
- **The Grey Glove**: Finely made, left on the wet stones of the Quay when the Hushed fled your lantern. A closed eye is stitched in silver thread on the cuff. You will see that eye again.
- **Gallery Side-Door Key**: The iron key to the little side door Fennick showed you on your first night in the Long Gallery. You walked your route backwards in the dark to reach it, and took Wren out while the Hushed searched an empty hall.
- **Chisel from the Hall of Faces**: A mason's chisel, its edge still bright, found at the foot of the eastern wall. With it you cut three hundred and twelve names back beneath their faces. Someone else once used one just like it to ruin a thirteenth.
- **Calder's Cipher Wheel**: Two brass discs on one pin, the outer ring stamped with digits and the inner with sounds. Ninety-four is a bear. Seventy-four is a car. Turn it slowly and the Counting House ledgers start telling their ugly little story.
- **Isolde's Silver Bolt**: A short crossbow bolt fletched in green, from the little silver crossbow Isolde Varre carries in her velvet. It went into the man who was aiming at you. She sent it back afterwards, polished, with a dinner invitation.
- **Warden's Seal Ring**: One of the thirteen rings of the Compact, cut with a lamp above an open eye. The old words on the Tongues Bridge kept it for five hundred years in a crack of white stone. Wren wears its twin on her thumb.
- **Ennick's Stolen Record**: The Order's own account of the night of the Tide, copied out in the Grand Hush's study and carried through the rain against Ennick's skin. One line is underlined twice: Find the courier.
- **The Widow's Rest Hood**: Rough grey sacking that smells of rosemary and river water. Isolde pulled it over your head on the eight-hundredth step and whispered the truth into the dark beneath it. You kept it. You are not sure why.
- **Cracked Mirror Shard**: A splinter of the Mirror Wards, cracked corner to corner. Look into it and a kitchen you never stood in looks back, warm and believable. You keep it behind a door in your mind marked: not mine.
- **The Waystation Register**: Twenty years of travellers' names in an old leather book from the crossroads above Fenwick. One entry is in your own handwriting. Delivered to the Archivist, Veyra. Returned by choice.
- **The Untouched Cup**: The silver cup of the Rite of Echoes, still full of grey. Sevrin Ashgrave looked at it for a long moment and pushed it away. Even the Hush has things he cannot bear to lose.
- **Ember of the Lamp of Ysolde**: A coal that fell from the great Lamp under the Archive dome on the Night of No Moon, when it caught fire for the first time in three hundred years. It is warm in your hand and has not gone out. It may never go out.

## Ledger Pages

Calder's twelve pages, in her small, fierce hand.

- **First Ledger Page**: Under the base of the last lamp on the Quay, wrapped in oilcloth. "Hold it as a picture or not at all. Words drift. Pictures anchor. Places hold. If you are reading this, you have found the first. There are eleven more. Trust no one who offers you peace."
- **Second Ledger Page**: Behind the frame of Annet Gale in the Long Gallery. "The city is a palace. I built it to be walked. I walked it every night so that I would never be the only one who knew the way. If you are reading this, walk it further than I did. The courier knows the road. Keep the courier safe."
- **Third Ledger Page**: Behind the little bronze lamp-hook beside the scratched face. "Forgive me. It was the only way to hide you."
- **Fourth Ledger Page**: Folded inside the spine of a Counting House ledger. "Count what they take, and you will know what they want. They do not want money. Money is only what they use. Watch the clocks."
- **Fifth Ledger Page**: Waiting on your pillow in the locked Archive. "They will try to frighten you, then flatter you, then buy you. When none of that works, they will try to make the city hate you. Do not let it make you hate the city."
- **Sixth Ledger Page**: Sewn into the lining of a Hushed robe, found by Isolde. "They will tell you I opened the gate. I did. Ask them why, and watch what they say. Then ask the Scriptorium."
- **Seventh Ledger Page**: In Ennick's bundle all along. "Now you know why. Do not forgive me yet. You do not know the price."
- **Eighth Ledger Page**: Pressed into your hand under the hood on the Widow's Rest. "Everyone you trust will be tested. Some will fail. Not all who seem to fail have failed."
- **Ninth Ledger Page**: Taken off the Grand Hush's desk by Ennick, without knowing what it was. "The courier and the heir. One carries the road, the other the way home. Do not let them separate you."
- **Tenth Ledger Page**: Pressed into the back cover of the waystation register. "You chose this once. You are allowed to choose it again."
- **Eleventh Ledger Page**: In Old Tansy's basket, under the bundles of rosemary. "If you are reading this, you have found me, and I no longer know you. I am sorry. It was the only safe place left. Look after my brother. He was the kindest of us."
- **Twelfth Ledger Page**: Never written down. Calder gave it to you herself, over two cups of rosemary tea. "That's the last lesson, I think. Not how to keep everything. How to choose."

## Trinkets

Keepsakes from the people of Veyra, for favours done.

- **Mosk's Ferry Token**: A worn bronze token stamped with a little boat. Show it at the Quay steps and Mosk ferries you free for a year, and tells you so every single time.
- **Tansy's Teacup**: A chipped cup that always smells faintly of rosemary tea, for the remembering. Tansy poured two of these the night she sang you the Lamplighter's Song.
- **Fennick's Key Tag**: A wooden tag on a loop of string, worn smooth by thirty-one years in a caretaker's pocket. It came with the spare key to the Gallery, and with Fennick's verdict: That'll hold for life.
- **The Backward Map**: A scrap of map Wren drew of your route, every arrow pointing the wrong way. Calder used to say that a route you can only walk forwards is a story, not a place.
- **Brennick Seed Cake**: A slice of the cake that arrived every week for a month, from the granddaughter of Aldo Brennick, harbour pilot. It never goes stale. Some kindnesses keep.
- **Kettering Ford Badge**: A tin road-warden's badge with a milestone and two crossed staves. Two brothers wore this badge once. Joss Hask told you about the other one, more words in a row than he had said all month.
- **Isolde's Scented Note**: Folded thick paper, sealed in green wax and scented with something expensive. Impressive. Tuesday, the Fenwick road, midnight. Bring the large one.
- **The Salt Guild's Second Book**: A small black book from under a Counting House floorboard, its clasp crusted with salt. Every Watch officer the Guild ever paid is in it. Wren carries the list in her head now, not on paper.
- **Pellam's Winding Key**: The brass key to the oldest clock in the market, the one that coughed, whirred and struck thirteen. Pellam's grandfather made it. Pellam had forgotten that until you remembered sixteen digits for him.
- **The Rook Card**: A playing card from Varre House, a black rook on a green field. Isolde taught you Rook with this deck, and how to lose a hand on purpose when it suits you.
- **The Riddle Stone**: The loose block that slid out of the Tongues Bridge parapet when you read its riddle a week later. What you learn today you own tomorrow; what you keep a week you keep for life.
- **Hennoweth Candle**: A stub of candle in a tin dish, left burning in a window. Hennoweth: the ache of a lamp left burning for someone who is not coming home. Mosk said it until he remembered her name. Hennet.
- **Brother Hollin's Quill**: A grey goose quill with grey ink dried on the nib, taken from the desk of the Grand Hush's secretary. Forgers always get small facts wrong. You caught all ten of his.
- **Ennick's Notebook**: A thin notebook tied with string, where Ennick first learned to look at his own mistakes. He stopped needing it after a week. It doesn't hurt as much as forgetting did.
- **Bree's Red Ribbon**: The hair ribbon of the champion of the Tidal Stair, handed over the evening you beat her by two steps. She demanded a rematch every evening for a month. She never stopped trying.
- **Masquerade Mask**: A green and gold half-mask on an ebony stick, from the ball at Varre House. Three hundred guests in twenty rooms, and you knew who stood where all night. Isolde may have to keep you.
- **The Two-List Slate**: A child's slate with two lists chalked side by side, one bright and one smudged nearly away. Keep the first. Forget the second. The mirror cracked like ice on a pond.
- **Wren's Carving Mallet**: The little wooden mallet Wren used over three nights to carve her own face back into the eastern wall of the Hall, and her name beneath it. Hello, she told it. It's been a while.
- **Stillwater Pebbles**: Three painted pebbles from the village square at Stillwater, where you taught the children to set a word in a place. The next morning, three of them still remembered. It is a small thing.
- **Ammerhold Milestone**: A palm-sized milestone from the top of the pass, carved with the road home. Hask checked you on every item of a month-old list up the mountain, then said, You'll do. From a road-warden, that is everything.
- **The Rite Coat**: Black wool lined with green silk, sent by Isolde with a note: For the Rite. Lose in this and I will have it back. She did not have it back.
- **Bundle of Rosemary**: Rosemary from Tansy's basket, tied with twine. She sang the last verse at last under the lamp and remembered, for one breath, that she had a brother.
- **The Autumn Leaf**: A leaf from the autumn, when you learned something you still hold three months on. That's yours now, Tansy said. Not the river, not the grey, not anybody. Remember that I said so.
- **The Circle's Lamp Token**: A bronze token stamped with a small lamp, ringed by six dots, one for each friend who coaches by the Quay. Wren says it opens nothing. It only says that you are expected.
- **The Keeper's Oath Medal**: Struck in bronze with the Lamp of Ysolde, given under the copper dome when Wren swore you in as a Keeper of Veyra. Nobody had walked the routes three hundred days in three centuries.

## Lost Treasures

Relics of the Drowned Years, brought up from the Crypt.

- **Ferryman's Bone Dice**: Two yellowed dice with eyes instead of pips. The ferrymen of the Drowned Years cast them for passengers who could not remember where they were going, and took whichever shore the dice chose.
- **Shard of the First Mirror**: Silver, older than the Mirror Wards, and it shows no face at all. Only rooms. The Order's first mirrors were cut from this one, and they never learned what it was trying to show them.
- **Warden's Compass**: Its needle does not point north. It points toward the nearest thing you have forgotten, and trembles when you are close. The Wardens carried them through the Tide like dogs on a lead.
- **Crown of a Nameless King**: Black gold, set with river-stones, sized for a small head. Somebody ruled the river-folk in the Drowned Years wearing this. Nobody, not even the crown, remembers who.
- **Ysolde's Wick**: A charred wick in a clay saucer, lit nine hundred years ago, and burning still with a flame no wider than a grain of rice. The songs say it was the first lamp of the Compact.
- **Tide Pearl**: A grey pearl, cold and heavy as a held breath. The river-folk believed every memory the Tide took sank to the bottom and was slowly wrapped in pearl. This one is warm on one side.
- **Mask of the Hollow Choir**: A smooth white face with no mouth. The choirs of the Drowned Years wore them to sing the songs no one could remember writing, and sang them perfectly, and forgot them when the masks came off.
- **The Undercroft Key**: Heavy black iron, its bow worked into twelve little sluice-wheels. It opens a door beneath the Lethe Gate that the Wardens walled up and then, very carefully, forgot.
- **Chart of the Drowned Stars**: A sky map drawn on fish-skin, full of stars that are no longer there. The Nameless Kings steered by them through the long fog, toward a shore they could not name.
- **First Phial of the Grey**: Lethewater, drawn from the river the night the Drowned Years began, and stoppered with black wax. It is the first grey. Whoever bottled it wanted, very badly, to forget something.
- **Heartstone of the Compact**: A red stone that beats, slowly, once a minute. The thirteen Wardens laid their hands on it to swear the Compact of Lamps. It still remembers every one of their names.
- **The Lamp of Ages**: The lamp the first river-folk carried out of the Drowned Years, before Ysolde, before the city, before anyone had a name to remember. Its light falls on things as they truly were.
- **Root Warden Halo**: A circular ring of glowing amber stone embedded with thick twisting vines and small pulsing red berries. This ancient barrier seals the root system that keeps the Undercroft from collapsing into the river below.
- **The Tide Count Tablet**: A long slab of dark blue slate covered in hundreds of scratched tally marks arranged in concentric circles around a central eye symbol. It records every drop of Lethe water that has seeped through the city foundations since the Drowned Years began.
- **Scriptorium Dust Chest**: A small lead box sealed with wax and filled with fine grey ash mixed with burnt parchment scraps and dried rosemary sprigs. Old Tansy keeps this hidden to preserve the scent of her lost memories before they fade completely into the white mist.
- **Mirror Shard Pile**: A heap of jagged silver glass fragments arranged on a velvet cloth that reflect no image but only show warm golden light where you stand. Isolde Varre uses these shards to hide her face from the Hushed spies who hunt for smugglers in the deep waterways.
- **Compact Fragment Tablet**: A chipped piece of bronze plate engraved with a single lamp icon and three crossed hammers that have been worn smooth by centuries of touch. It is one of the original thirteen stones carved when Ysolde founded the Lamp Wardens to protect Veyra.
- **Grey Bottle Case**: A wooden crate lined with soft grey cloth holding dozens of small glass bottles filled with a thick opaque silver liquid that swirls slowly inside. Brother Ennick stores these vials of the grey drink for those who wish to forget their pain without losing their names entirely.
- **Warm Silver Pool**: A shallow pool of clear liquid metal that glows with a soft warm silver light and feels like bathwater when stepped into barefoot. Mosk ferries the most precious memories across this water to keep them safe from the eroding Tide above ground.

## Seals

Wax seals pressed for deeds worth remembering.

- **Seal of First Light**: Pressed in amber wax over a small flame. Every Keeper's ledger begins with one lamp, lit once.
- **Seal of the Cornerstone**: A squared stone in green wax. Ten rooms you know with your eyes shut, and a route through them that is yours.
- **Seal of the Clean Sweep**: A broom in blue wax. Every item, every one, and nothing left on the floor for the Tide.
- **Seal of the Backward Walk**: A turning arrow in violet wax. If you can only walk a route forwards, it is a story, not a place.
- **Seal of It Stayed**: An anchor in river-blue wax. A night's sleep, and the picture was still there in the morning, waiting.
- **Seal of A Week Later**: A seven in green wax, one for every day it held. What you keep a week, the bridge says, you keep for life.
- **Seal of the Rekindled Lamp**: A lamp relit, in red wax. The Quay kept while you were gone. So did Wren.
- **Seal of the Steady Flame**: A tall still flame in amber wax. Seven days in fourteen. A habit is a lamp you do not have to relight.
- **Seal of the Honest Ledger**: An open book in brown wax. You looked at your own mistakes without flinching, three times. Ennick would be proud.
- **Seal of the Sharper Edge**: A rising star in silver-grey wax. The drills grew harder because you grew faster.
- **Seal of the Restored Quay**: A lamp-post in gold wax, the first of forty-four. For the first time in three hundred years, the Tide rose and took nothing.
- **Seal of the Face Reader**: A face in rose wax. Eight names fastened to eight faces, so firmly they will never come loose.
- **Seal of the Number Smith**: A hammer on an anvil in iron-black wax. Numbers into pictures, faster than a Guild courier can change his code.
- **Seal of Safe Keeping**: A little padlock in teal wax. A copy of everything you have built, kept where the river cannot reach.
- **Seal of the Month Holder**: Pressed for three delayed recalls passed a full month after learning. Wren says most of the city forgets a thing in a week. You held three of them for thirty days.
- **Seal of the Long Memory**: Pressed for a gate recalled at 70% or better three months after you passed it. The Tide came up ninety times over those streets, and still they stood.
- **Midsummer Seal**: Pressed at the turn of your year: six districts restored and twenty delayed recalls passed. Calder kept one like it on her desk, and never once explained it.
- **Seal of the Whole City**: Pressed for holding what you learned for a month or more in six different skills. Pictures, routes, faces, numbers, words: the city does not run on one trick, and neither do you.
- **Seal of the Half Year**: Pressed for a gate recalled at 70% or better six months after you passed it. Mosk says nothing on the river lasts half a year. He has been wrong before, though he would not like you to say so.
- **Seal of the Long Road**: Pressed at the far end of the Open Roads: nine districts restored and forty delayed recalls passed. Hask looked at it for a long time and said it was a good, plain seal.
- **Seal of the Keeper's Year**: Pressed on the morning after the Night of No Moon: all twelve districts restored and sixty delayed recalls passed. There is a lamp on it, and under the lamp, very small, your own name.

## Keepsakes

Small precious things, one for each stretch of memories that held.

- **Ysolde's First Coin**: A tarnished bronze disc stamped with a single flame icon. It was the first payment made for lighting Lamplighters Quay after the Compact.
- **Sevrin's Grey Vial**: A stoppered glass tube filled with opaque silver liquid. Sevrin Ashgrave keeps it to remember the taste of pain before forgetting it entirely.
- **Mosk's Iron Bolt**: Rust colored iron fastener shaped like a river otter skull. Mosk uses this bolt to seal his ferry door when he expects trouble from the Tide.
- **Amphitheatre Shard**: A jagged piece of pale marble that hums faintly in silence. It was pulled from the Amphitheatre walls after a storm erased all sound for one night.
- **Gate Salt Vial**: A tiny clay pot holding coarse white crystals that smell of rain. Isolde Varre stole this salt to prove the Lethe Gate could be crossed without losing memory.
- **Wrens Card Clip**: A small brass clip shaped like a folded paper boat. Wren uses it to keep her most urgent notecards from fluttering into the mist.
- **Market Cog Fragment**: A bronze gear with one missing tooth and engraved numbers. It fell from the Clockwork Market clocktower during the Day of Silent Chimes.
- **Bridge Pin**: Riveted steel pin wrapped in a strip of woven blue cloth. Joss Hask hammered this into Tongues Bridge to hold back a wave of white mist.
- **Ward Lens**: A circular shard of polished obsidian with a silver rim. The Mirror Wards use it to reflect the Tide away from the Scriptorium shelves.
- **Drowned Shell**: Rusted bronze coin fused into a spiral sea shell shape. Fennick found this in the Undercroft where river folk traded secrets for safe passage during the Drowned Years

## Old Documents

Papers from Veyra's past, found as each district comes back. Each one can be read.

- **The Salt Ledger of the Third Drowning**: The salt eats the corners of this book now, but I can still see the tallies. We agreed to trade three sacks of dried kelp for one crate of river clay before the mist rolled in thick as wool. The Last Ferryman marked his name with a thumbprint of red mud. He promised us safe passage across the black water if we left our silver behind at the bank. We did not leave it. Now the water holds more than just fish. It holds what we owed and what we kept. Do not trust the quiet parts of the river. They are listening for change that never comes back to shore.
- **Hesper's Foundation Stone**: I cut this slab from a king who never had a name. The stone was cold and heavy with old silence, but it held true under my chisel. Here I set the first corner of the Tidal Stair. Let the river rise or fall; this block stays put. We build on what is buried so that we may stand above it. No one remembers the kings who built these tombs, only their weight remains in our hands now. I mark my work with red ochre and a small lamp for the dark to come. If you find this stone loose later, do not move it. The stair needs its foundation more than the dead need their rest. Hesper signed his name below the line before the mortar dried.
- **The Compact of Lamps**: The river Lethe does not ask permission before it takes your name. It simply washes away until you are a stranger to yourself. We cannot stop the Tide, but we can hold back the dark with light and truth. I, Ysolde of the Lamp, set this seal in wax over thirteen silver rings. Each ring belongs to one district of Veyra. From this day forward, no Keeper may sleep while their lantern flickers. You must tend the flame, guard the words, and keep our history bright against the white mist. If you forget your duty, you join the grey silence below. Keep the lamp lit.
- **Recipe for The Grey, Batch 402**: Batch 402 requires precision. Measure three parts dried valerian root against one part river clay ash. The ratio must be exact to avoid nausea before the forgetting takes hold. Add a single drop of distilled lethe water from the Undercroft cistern, no more. Stir until the liquid turns the color of wet slate. Do not taste it yourself, Sevrin knows the temptation is strong but you are only hands now. The pain leaves in ten minutes and stays gone for an hour. If they ask what it tastes like, tell them rain on stone. Keep the vials wrapped in oilskin so no one smells the bitter herbs underneath. This batch serves forty souls who wish to be quiet again tonight.
- **Map of the Long Gallery, Hall 9**: The Long Gallery holds nine halls under one long roof. Hall Nine stands at the far end near the river wall where the light fades to grey sepia. This map shows what remains after the Tide took its share. You see empty frames in white lines against dark canvas, waiting for memories that have not yet returned. Notice how a whole section is missing entirely here on the chart. That gap was never painted out by mistake. It was carved away with care and intent. Behind those blank canvases stood Old Tansy keeping her name safe from prying eyes and hungry tides. We mark this space so you know exactly where to look if you wish to find what she left behind for someone brave enough to ask the right questions about who she truly was before she became a legend in rosemary tea.
- **Bridge Toll Receipts for Foreign Tongues**: Toll Receipt No. 492 through 503. Paid in full for silent passage over Tongues Bridge during the High Mist. The payer agrees to hold their true name back from the water and the wind until they reach solid ground on the far bank. These slips are proof that Isolde Varre did not hear what was spoken, nor will she repeat it later. Each stamp fades if you press too hard, so handle them gently with dry fingers. If a slip dissolves completely before you cross, your debt is paid and your secret is safe in her keeping. Do not burn these papers near the lamps. The ink remembers heat even when the paper forgets. Keep them flat in a coat pocket or inside a hat brim until you are safely across.
- **The Song of the Empty Seats**: The bass line is gone now. Just a ragged hole where the low notes used to hum against your chest. We sang it when the mist took everything at once. Twelve districts, empty of their own names. I remember the silence after. The kind that hurts like a bruise forming in slow time. Wren held my hand so tight her knuckles turned white, but she could not tell me why we were standing there. She had forgotten the reason for the song before the first note faded from the air. Now the vellum is thin as old skin. The ink blurs if you breathe on it too hard. Do not let them tear out more of us. Hold what remains in your mouth like a stone, even if you cannot say why it matters to keep it there until morning comes back to wash the grey away from our eyes and hands.
- **Wren's Note on the Undercroft Key**: I found it tucked into *The Weight of Water*. Don’t tell Tansy she left her rosemary behind again. The key isn’t locked away in a vault. It’s under the roots. Look for the oldest bush by the Scriptorium wall, the one with leaves so dark they look black at night. Dig there. I know it sounds silly to bury steel beneath plant life, but the earth keeps secrets better than iron does. The mist is rising fast and we have no time left for clever locks that can be picked or broken. Just go down and find what Ysolde hid before she forgot why she was hiding it. Please be careful with your hands.

## Lost and Found

Odd things people lost, turned up while you polished your relics.

- **A small round glass vial filled with pale yellow liquid and sealed with wax.**: Wren needs this vial to prove that Old Tansy is actually Calder the lost archivist before the Tide erases her name.
- **A jagged piece of tarnished brass shaped like a compass rose with one missing arm.**: Joss Hask asks you to find this shard so he can repair his broken map and keep the smuggling routes secret from Isolde Varre.
- **A flat grey slate tile etched with the name Ennick in fading white chalk ink.**: Brother Ennick needs this tag returned to him so he remembers who he was before becoming a monk of the Hushed Order.
- **An oval stone token covered in green river moss and worn smooth by years of handling.**: Mosk requests you find his lost ferry token which is actually a key that opens the Undercroft entrance at high tide.
- **A heavy black iron key shaped like a bird with outstretched wings and no teeth on the bit.**: Fennick wants this key to unlock the back door of the Long Gallery where he hides the true portraits of the Nameless Kings.
- **A small cylindrical block of dark red wax used for stamping official documents from the Counting House.**: The Grand Hush needs you to steal this stump so she can forge a letter that will let her cross Tongues Bridge without being detained.
- **A single brown leather glove with three missing fingers and a faint smell of rosemary tea.**: Wren asks you to find this glove because it holds the only physical proof that Old Tansy has been traveling in time during the Drowned Years.
- **A curved piece of unglazed clay from a street lamp base painted with chipping white geometric patterns.**: Isolde Varre wants this shard delivered to Ysolde's grave so she can finally understand why the Compact of Lamps was broken centuries ago.
- **A torn corner of a decorative paper fan printed with blue ink illustrations of the river Lethe flowing uphill.**: Sevrin Ashgrave needs you to remember what is drawn on this fragment because it describes the exact moment the Tide first rose in Veyra.
- **A small carved wooden head painted with closed eyes and wearing a tiny crown of wire and dried flowers.**: The Hall of Faces keeper asks you to find this doll so she can restore her own memory of who she was before becoming a Keeper.

## Keeper's Gear

What a Keeper carries, earned as your skills grow.

- **River Glass Lamp**: A squat amber glass vessel with a copper ring handle and a thick wick. The oil inside glows faintly blue when the mist gets too close.
- **Salt Chalk Sticks**: Two short grey sticks wrapped in rough linen that leave a shimmering trail on stone. They mark safe paths where memory has already been washed away by the Tide.
- **Brine Satchel**: A waterproof pouch made of oiled fish leather with brass clasps shaped like anchors. It holds tools that must never get wet from the river Lethe.
- **Tide Map Case**: A round box carved from dark driftwood with a hinged lid covered in scratched compass points. Inside are maps that change as the city's districts shift and heal.
- **Wick Trimmer**: Small iron nippers with wooden handles worn smooth by years of use. They cut away burnt cotton so the lantern flame stays steady and bright against the fog.
- **Memory Vial Set**: A row of five tiny glass vials filled with liquids ranging from clear to deep violet. Each one holds a scent or taste needed to restore a specific district's feeling.
- **Ledger Pouch**: A slim leather case holding blank pages bound by silver rings and a stubby ink pen. Wren keeps her notes here so the wind cannot scatter them away into the mist.
- **Rosemary Tea Bag**: A small muslin sack filled with dried green herbs that smells of sharp pine and old books. Old Tansy uses it to clear her head before she helps a Keeper remember too much.
- **Anchor Ribbon**: A strip of heavy red wool woven into the Keeper's belt loop. It ties down loose thoughts so they do not float up with the rising river water.

## Trial Prizes

Found behind the District Trials and the sealed vaults, for what you could still recall.

- **The Warden's Ledger Fragment**: A torn page from the logbook under the Hall of Faces, with a brass corner and a frayed ribbon. Ten names in a neat hand, and one more in the margin, crossed out and written again.
- **A Salt Guild Dial**: One brass dial from the Salt Guild vault, its knurled edge worn smooth by clerks who carried the code home in their heads. Isolde unscrewed it with a hairpin.
- **The Market Mainspring**: The old mainspring of the market clock, coiled in its brass barrel. It was replaced long ago, but Mosk kept it in a drawer. He says a spring remembers how it was wound.
- **The Gargoyle's Stone**: A smooth grey river stone with a small friendly face carved on it. The eldest gargoyle of the Tongues Bridge gives one to every traveller who still knows the old words a week later.
- **The Saved Scroll**: A scroll from the high chest of the Sunken Scriptorium, tied with blue ribbon and sealed with a drop of amber wax. It stayed dry because you held its timeline for a day.
- **The Quay Vault Lamp**: A small lamp on an iron hook from the vault in the Quay wall. Its flame is the size of a fingernail and has not gone out since the Wardens lit it.
- **The Cellar Tablet**: A square clay tablet stamped with a lamp, found in the cellar vault under the clock tower. It is the key to its own door, which the Wardens thought was a good joke.
- **The Mirror Key**: A bronze key with a bow shaped like a lamp, from behind the dark mirror. It was waiting for someone who could keep a tablet for a whole month.
